chunks: Due to the saying of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: “The full siblings from the same mother are more entitled to inheritance than the half-siblings from different mothers.”

If the deceased leaves full sisters, paternal sisters, and a paternal nephew, then the full sisters receive two-thirds, and the remainder is returned to them, because they are the closer relatives. If he leaves a paternal brother and a nephew from both parents, then the entire estate belongs to the paternal brother, because he is nearer in degree. If he leaves a full brother and a maternal brother, the maternal brother receives one-sixth, and the remainder belongs to the full brother. If he leaves full brothers and sisters together with a maternal sister, the maternal sister receives one-sixth, and the remainder is divided among the full siblings, with the male receiving the share of two females. If he leaves a full sister and a maternal brother or sister, then the maternal sibling receives one-sixth, and the full sister takes the remainder. If he leaves two maternal brothers or two maternal sisters, or more than that, along with full siblings, then the maternal siblings receive one-third equally among themselves, and the remainder belongs to the full siblings. A maternal sibling, whether male or female, if only one, receives one-sixth; if they are more than one, whether male or female, they receive one-third. They are not increased beyond one-third, nor reduced below one-sixth when there is only one.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then each one of the two shall have a sixth; but if they are more than that, they are partners in one-third.”

If he leaves a paternal brother, a maternal brother, and a full brother, then the maternal brother receives one-sixth, the remainder belongs to the full brother, and the paternal brother is excluded. If he leaves maternal siblings, full siblings, and paternal siblings, then the maternal siblings receive one-third, with male and female equal in that share, and the remainder belongs to the full siblings, with the male receiving the share of two females, and the paternal siblings are excluded. If he leaves a maternal sister, a full sister, and a paternal sister, the maternal sister receives one-sixth, the remainder belongs to the full sister, and the paternal sister is excluded. If he leaves two maternal sisters, two full sisters, and two paternal sisters, then the two maternal sisters receive one-third equally, and the remainder belongs to the two full sisters, while the two paternal sisters are excluded. If he leaves a full sister, maternal brothers and sisters, and a son of a full brother, then the maternal siblings receive one-third equally between male and female, and the remainder belongs to the full sister, while the son of the full brother is excluded. If he leaves a paternal brother and a nephew from the mother, then the entire estate belongs to the paternal brother. If he leaves a maternal brother and a nephew from the father and mother, then the entire estate belongs to the maternal brother, and the nephew from the father and mother is excluded.

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan erred in this issue and held that the maternal brother receives his designated one-sixth, and the remainder goes to the son of the full brother, arguing with a weak proof that the son of the full brother stands in the place of the full brother who would have been entitled to the whole estate by the Book, and that he also has the added tie through the mother. The compiler of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said that the son of the brother only takes the place of the brother when no brother exists; if a brother is present, he does not take that place, just as a grandchild is treated as a child only when the deceased has no child or parents. If qiyas were valid in the religion of Allah, then in the case of a paternal brother and a nephew from both parents, the whole estate would go to the nephew by analogy with a paternal uncle and a cousin from both parents; but this ruling rests on a transmitted report from the Imams عليهم السلام, to whom submission is obligatory. The passage then continues with further inheritance rulings concerning nephews, nieces, descendants of siblings, and their precedence over uncles, aunts, maternal uncles, and maternal aunts, establishing that descendants of siblings, even if remote, have stronger entitlement than descendants of the grandfather, and that the children of a sister follow the same rule.

key_terms.أَعْيَانُ بَنِي الْأُمِّ: full siblings who share the same mother, used here for those with stronger inheritance priority
key_terms.الْقِيَاسُ: analogical reasoning, rejected here as a basis for these inheritance rulings
key_terms.فَرَائِضَ الْمَوَارِيثِ: the divinely assigned rules and shares of inheritance
key_terms.كَلَالَةً: a deceased person leaving neither parents nor children in the inheritance context
key_terms.وُلْدِ الْعَلَّاتِ: half-siblings through the father with different mothers

ai.seo_question: How are inheritance shares divided among full, paternal, and maternal siblings in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage sets out detailed rulings on the inheritance shares of full siblings, paternal siblings, maternal siblings, and the descendants of siblings, emphasizing precedence by closeness of kinship and line of relation. It also cites the Qur'anic ruling on kalalah and rejects qiyas in determining inheritance shares where transmitted teachings from the Imams عليهم السلام establish the law.
